@R44VC0RP I think I figured it out. I'm using Tmux in Ghostty with these configs:

```
set-option -g default-terminal "tmux-256color"
set-option -sa terminal-overrides ',xterm-256color:RGB,*:sitm=\E[3m:ritm=\E[23m'
```

When I use Opencode outside of Tmux in _just_ Ghostty, I have the `system` option in `/theme` and it loads automatically from my `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`.

When I jump back into Tmux, the option's gone and it falls back to the default Opencode theme.

I guess this is all to say, I think it has to do with terminal color settings. These were working with `< 1.0` for me (hadn't updated in a while until end of last week).

Quick update from our side: After our [earlier comment](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/6651#issuecomment-3841762673) about multi-provider research, we discovered that our actual issue was a separate config bug — agent frontmatter fields (`description`, `tools`, etc.) were leaking into LLM API requests and causing provider rejections. We filed that separately as PR #12967.

So to be clear: **model tiers were never the problem for us.** We actually built our entire agent system around `model_tier` (Solution C) in a local dev build of PR #11377, and it works extremely well. We're running 15 agents across 5 providers (Anthropic, Zen/OpenRouter, Perplexity, xAI, Google) with per-agent tier mappings, and the orchestrator's ability to dynamically select `quick`/`standard`/`advanced` based on task complexity has been a game-changer for cost control.

**Strongly in favor of merging #11377.** The tier abstraction is the right design — simple for the LLM to reason about, fully user-configurable, and it composes perfectly with multi-provider setups. Great work @mcking-07, this is a well-thought-out feature.

These issues share the common theme of web UI performance/streaming problems, especially in remote or proxied deployments. The root causes appear to be:
1. SSE stream architecture keeping idle responses for minutes (doesn't work well over remote/proxied connections)
2. Inefficient event broadcasting (all events to all clients, then filtered client-side)
3. Reverse proxy compatibility not optimized for this use case

This issue appears to be a duplicate of #12441: [Project avatar fallback doesn't support emoji characters](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/12441), which was recently closed.

Both issues describe the same root cause: JavaScript string indexing returns individual UTF-16 code units, but emojis use surrogate pairs. When using code like `[0]` to get the first character of an emoji, it returns only the first half of the surrogate pair, resulting in a broken character display.

Since #12441 was already closed, please check if the fix has been deployed or if this remains an open issue.

- #12834: Random TUI freeze/hang with process continuing in background
